title: Passage from sheaves to complexes
statement:
Suppose that, for a separated finite-type map $f:X_0\to Y_0$, every
mixed Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ of weights at most $v$ has
$R^af_!\mathcal F$ mixed of weights at most $v+a$, for every $a$.
Then $Rf_!$ carries $D_{\le w}(X_0)$ into $D_{\le w}(Y_0)$.

proof.text: Use the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and let $K\in D_{\le w}(X_0)$. Write $X,Y$ for the geometric fibers of $X_0,Y_0$, and $f_k:X\to Y$ for the base change of $f$. The finite-type hypotheses on the geometric fibers follow from [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change], and $f_k$ is separated and finite type by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Both $X_0,Y_0$ are finite type over $k_0$ by the finite-field conventions, and $X,Y$ are finite type over $k$ by the preceding base-change lemma. Each field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal). Applying [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] to these four structure morphisms shows that $X_0,Y_0,X,Y$ are Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] all four are quasi-separated. In particular the hypothesis on the original schemes in [lem-zl-weil-shriek-shift-compatibility] is satisfied. All truncations below are in $D^b_c(X,\Qlb)$, and $Rf_{k!}$ has bounded constructible values by [lem-zl-field-shriek-lower-bound]. Equip each output $Rf_{k!}M$ of a Weil complex $(M,\theta_M)$ with its canonical Weil structure $Rf_{k!}(\theta_M)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,M}$ of [lem-fix-weil-operations], which applies on this domain because $Rf_{k!}$ preserves bounded constructibility. Thus no torsion small-etale coefficient category is substituted for the field-coefficient category.

source.place: Opening: the exact compact-support functor, with its field-coefficient domain made explicit

proof.text:
By the bounded standard t-structure and constructible truncations of [prop-constructible-truncations], choose integers $A\le B$ with $\operatorname{For}K\in D^{\ge A}\cap D^{\le B}$. Put $K_b=\tau^{\le b}K$ for $A-1\le b\le B$. Then $K_{A-1}=0$ and $K_B\simeq K$. For $A\le b\le B$, the standard truncation triangle for $K_b$ at $b-1$ is
$$\operatorname{For}K_{b-1}\longrightarrow\operatorname{For}K_b\longrightarrow\mathcal H^b(\operatorname{For}K)[-b]\longrightarrow\operatorname{For}K_{b-1}[1].$$
Indeed its third term is $\tau^{\ge b}\tau^{\le b}\operatorname{For}K=\mathcal H^b(\operatorname{For}K)[-b]$, by the formula defining cohomology in [prop-constructible-truncations]. The Weil structures come as follows. The geometric Frobenius $g_X$ is a scheme automorphism of $X$, so by [prop-constructible-truncations] $Lg_X^*$ commutes with $\tau^{\le m},\tau^{\ge m}$; hence applying $Lg_X^*$ to the truncation triangle of any $M$ at $m$ gives a triangle with terms in $D^{\le m}$ and $D^{\ge m+1}$. By the uniqueness in clause (1) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] there is a unique isomorphism $c:Lg_X^*\tau^{\le m}M\simeq\tau^{\le m}Lg_X^*M$ compatible with the maps to $Lg_X^*M$, and $\theta_{\tau^{\le m}M}=\tau^{\le m}(\theta_M)\circ c$ is the induced Weil structure; similarly for $\tau^{\ge m}$. By this uniqueness and naturality of $\tau^{\le m}$, the three objects and the first two natural arrows are Weil objects and Weil morphisms. These are triangles in the underlying constructible category; no triangulated structure on the category of fixed pairs is assumed.

source.place: Opening truncation construction, expanded as its finite tower

proof.text:
Let $F_b=\mathcal H^b(K)$, with its induced Weil structure. By [def-weil-complex-weights], $F_b$ is mixed of weights at most $w+b$. Apply [lem-zl-weil-shriek-shift-compatibility] with $\Lambda=\Qlb$, input $F_b$ and shift $r=-b$, using the quasi-separatedness of $X_0,Y_0$ checked in step 1. Its comparison intertwines the canonical exchange Weil structures. Taking $n$th cohomology and using $\mathcal H^n(M[-b])=\mathcal H^{n-b}(M)$ therefore gives an isomorphism of Weil sheaves
$$\mathcal H^n(Rf_{k!}(F_b[-b]))\simeq\mathcal H^{n-b}(Rf_{k!}F_b).$$
If $n-b\ge0$, the hypothesis of the item, applied with $v=w+b$ and $a=n-b$, makes the right side mixed of weights at most $(w+b)+(n-b)=w+n$. If $n-b<0$, it is zero by the lower-bound assertion of [lem-zl-field-shriek-lower-bound], applied to the heart object $F_b$. The zero sheaf has the empty mixed filtration of [def-weil-punctual-weights], so it has every upper weight bound. Hence the displayed sheaf has bound $w+n$ for all $n$.

source.place: Middle: the bound on the cohomology-sheaf pieces, including negative higher-image indices

proof.text:
Apply the exact triangulated functor $Rf_{k!}$ of [lem-zl-field-shriek-lower-bound] to each underlying triangle of step 2. In the target standard t-structure of [prop-constructible-truncations], clause (5) of [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] gives the exact sequence in the constructible heart
$$\mathcal H^n(Rf_{k!}K_{b-1})\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal H^n(Rf_{k!}K_b)\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal H^n(Rf_{k!}(F_b[-b])).$$
The maps $u,v$ are Weil morphisms: the truncation arrows were Weil morphisms, and for a Weil morphism $\phi:M\to M'$ naturality of the exchange $\operatorname{Ex}_!$ gives $Rf_{k!}(\phi)\circ Rf_{k!}(\theta_M)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,M}=Rf_{k!}(\theta_{M'})\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,M'}\circ Lg_Y^*Rf_{k!}(\phi)$, so $Rf_{k!}(\phi)$ is a Weil morphism for the canonical structures of [lem-fix-weil-operations]. Taking cohomology commutes with Frobenius pullback by [prop-constructible-truncations]. Exactness is therefore an exactness statement for these Weil sheaves, whose kernels and images exist in the abelian category specified by [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand]. Only this three-term segment is needed, so no boundary-map equivariance or spectral-sequence convergence is being inferred from a torsion $Rf_*$ statement.

source.place: Truncation construction and subquotient/extension argument; exactness is BBD 1.3.6

proof.text:
Induct on $b=A-1,A,\ldots,B$ to prove that $\mathcal H^n(Rf_{k!}K_b)$ is mixed of weights at most $w+n$ for every $n$. At $b=A-1$ it is zero: an exact additive functor sends the zero object to zero, and the empty filtration gives its bound [def-weil-punctual-weights]. For the induction step fix $n$. Put $U=\operatorname{im}u$ and $V=\operatorname{im}v$ for the maps in step 4. Exactness gives
$$0\longrightarrow U\longrightarrow\mathcal H^n(Rf_{k!}K_b)\longrightarrow V\longrightarrow0.$$
Here $U$ is a Weil quotient of $\mathcal H^n(Rf_{k!}K_{b-1})$, which has bound $w+n$ by induction, and $V$ is a Weil subsheaf of the last term in step 4, which has that bound by step 3. Clause (1) of [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand] gives the bound for $U,V$, and clause (2) gives it for their extension. This completes the finite induction. At $b=B$, the Weil isomorphism $K_B\simeq K$ identifies its output with $Rf_!K$. The defining cohomological inequalities of [def-weil-complex-weights] now say $Rf_!K\in D_{\le w}(Y_0)$, as required.

source.place: Final passage from subquotients and extensions to the complex weight bound
